gates.reason: Filesystem access is read-only, workflow filenames come from directory enumeration, and symlinked directories are not recursively followed; no path-traversal, command execution, secrets egress, or other active security concern was found.
The coverage detector scans entire workflow YAML files as undifferentiated text, so non-executable YAML fields can falsely count suites as CI-wired.
This is a bounded CI utility, not hot-path or shipped runtime code; it performs one scripts-tree traversal and one pass over workflow files.
The test contains no authentication, filesystem mutation, untrusted command execution, client surface, secrets handling, or deployment configuration.
The purported synthetic workflow test never supplies or parses a workflow and therefore does not exercise collectWiredSuites or protect the detector's executable-field boundary.
This small CI-only test suite is not hot-path code and introduces no runtime surface requiring a probe or budget.

findings.title: Non-executable workflow text can falsely prove a test suite is CI-wired
findings.what: collectWiredSuites applies suite-reference and npm-invocation regexes to the complete comment-stripped YAML document rather than only executable jobs.*.steps[*].run values. A path or `npm run` string in an inert field such as `env`, `name`, or metadata is treated as execution, allowing the gate to report coverage for a suite that no workflow runs. The test labeled as a synthetic workflow test does not construct a workflow or call collectWiredSuites, so this false-positive boundary is untested.
findings.fix: Parse each workflow as YAML and inspect only executable `jobs.*.steps[*].run` strings (including their block-scalar contents), then replace the placeholder test with a minimal temporary workflow fixture that calls collectWiredSuites. Include both a real `run` step and inert fields containing suite/npm text.
findings.acceptance: A test with a workflow containing only `env: { NOTE: "node --test scripts/foo.test.mjs" }` reports `scripts/foo.test.mjs` as unwired, while adding `steps: [{ run: "node --test scripts/foo.test.mjs" }]` reports it wired; equivalent cases for inert and executable `npm run test:foo` text also pass.
findings.verifyNote: Re-read scripts/check-test-suite-coverage.mjs:143-161 and scripts/check-test-suite-coverage.test.mjs:63-88 at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. A workflow containing `env: NOTE: "node --test scripts/foo.test.mjs"` and no executable run command is still scanned wholesale and marks the suite wired. The purported synthetic workflow test does not invoke collectWiredSuites, so the defect remains unguarded.
